title: Rome: having Scripture is not enough — you need its true sense, hence tradition
source_text: XL. Rursus instant adversarii, non satis est Scripturam in manibus habere, sed necesse est ut verum illius sensum teneamus. Nec enim fidei regula proprie sunt verba Scripturae, sed potius Scripturae sensus a Spiritu sancto intentus. Atqui verus Scripturae sensus ex sola Scriptura haberi non potest. Nam Scriptura saepissime ambigua & perplexa est, ut, nisi ab aliquo qui errare non possit explicetur, non possit intelligi: nec certi esse possimus de vero Scripturae sensu, nisi accedat traditio. Igitur Sola Scriptura non sufficit.
pass_a_gloss: Again the adversaries press, it is not enough to have Scripture in hand, but it is necessary that we hold its true sense. For the rule of faith is not properly the words of Scripture, but rather the sense of Scripture intended by the Holy Spirit. But the true sense of Scripture cannot be had from Scripture alone. For Scripture is very often ambiguous and perplexed, so that, unless it be explained by someone who cannot err, it cannot be understood: nor can we be certain of the true sense of Scripture, unless tradition come in. Therefore Scripture alone does not suffice.
pass_b_english: Rome presses again: owning the book is not enough — faith needs Scripture's true Spirit-intended sense.
Words alone are not the rule; the sense is.
That sense, they say, cannot come from Scripture alone, because the text is often ambiguous.
Without an infallible explainer — tradition — certainty fails; therefore sola Scriptura fails.
